A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bézier Splatting work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original vectorization quality, runtime measurements, and ablations, including DIV2K and Kodak results in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains original vectorization experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, runtime analyses, layer-wise optimization results, and SVG editing demonstrations.

M1.justification: v3 adds an SVG export procedure (Appendix B) and a LIVE-style layer-wise optimization variant (Section 4.3). Appendix C also reports uniform closed-region opacity, replacing v1 Section 4.3's three-opacity interpolation. These substantially extend the available procedures and revise closed-curve parameterization, while retaining the underlying splatting rasterizer.

E1.justification: DIV2K, Kodak, Clipart1K, and Danbooregion already appear in v1, so the image-domain coverage is retained. v3 extends demonstrated tasks through SVG conversion and primitive editing, including removal, movement, deformation, replication, and recoloring in Figure 6.

E2.justification: LIVSS is added as an evaluated closed-curve comparator in DIV2K Table 2 and qualitative comparisons. DiffVG and LIVE remain benchmark baselines. Newly cited O&R and SGLIVE are not reported as additional benchmark comparators.

E3.justification: The DIV2K subsampling, reconstruction metrics, and core iteration budgets remain unchanged. v3 revises the stated closed-curve pruning cutoff from 9,200 steps to stopping for the final 1,000 iterations, changes Figure 1's hardware from A100 to RTX 4090, and adds closed-curve Kodak evaluation and controlled interpolation-count/runtime measurements.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the open-curve pruning ablation with a closed-curve comparison of no strategy, pruning/densification, and layer-wise optimization. Appendix A adds runtime scaling and stage breakdowns, alongside layer-wise case studies. The original opacity ablation and watercolor curve-count study survive as Table 5 and Figure 8, while v1 Figure 5's component-removal visualization disappears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3's additional timing measurements do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes open forward time from 7.2 to 4.5 ms and closed backward time from 15.7 to 24.58 ms. Closed DIV2K results also change: at 1,024 curves, PSNR becomes 23.45 instead of 23.55 and optimization time becomes 8.6 minutes instead of 3m25s. v3 adds LIVSS, closed-Kodak, layer-wise, and scaling results, while removing the 2,048-curve columns from the quality tables. Changed or incompletely matched settings prevent interpreting these replacements as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the Bézier/Bernstein definitions, interpolation, Gaussian scales and covariance, alpha blending, and optimization objective. Expanded sampling explanations and export pseudocode do not introduce a new proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The fast differentiable rasterization and adaptive curve-placement contributions remain central. v3 adds explicit standard-SVG interoperability to the abstract, raises the forward-speed claim from approximately 20× to 30×, and replaces the abstract's 10× optimization claim with an unspecified significant speedup; the 150× backward claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of LIVSS's difficulty with ambiguous semantic regions, the quality-versus-time tradeoff of layer-wise optimization, and sampling versus splatting bottlenecks. Appendix C motivates uniform closed-region attributes through SVG compatibility. The existing convexity and closed-curve computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and explicit SVG construction instructions, including coordinate conversion, cubic path commands, sigmoid-derived colors, and output opacity. These improve documentation of the added export capability; the core optimizer, learning-rate, initialization, and pruning implementation details are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to O&R, LIVSS, and SGLIVE and positions Bézier Splatting as a renderer compatible with existing topology-aware vectorization strategies. The broader vectorization and Gaussian-splatting research positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the overall section sequence are retained. v3 edits the title, introduction, and comparison discussion, reorders open/closed sampling explanations, and redistributes main-text ablations into Appendices A and C. These are localized narrative changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout and substantially redesigns its visual presentation. The teaser and image galleries are replaced or reorganized, comparison panels gain LIVSS, new editing and layer-wise figures appear, and tables are restructured alongside new ablation and runtime displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 better supports practical usability through an explicit SVG conversion procedure and editing demonstrations, and clarifies efficiency tradeoffs through layer-wise and runtime analyses. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 6 claims open-curve coverage despite containing closed-curve rows, and Appendix C's uniform-opacity setting is not reconciled with Section 3.2's separate-opacity description. The added evidence supports a bounded overall improvement, not a demonstrated across-the-board performance gain.
